utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Back to where we are. Can we have the appearances, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours. As I believe the Presiding Judge has been informed, lead counsel Mr. Ostberg is away Monday through Wednesday for an academic event. He will return on Thursday. Meanwhile the Prosecution will continue. Also I believe your Honours and most people in the courtroom know, Mr. Ostberg is going to be leaving at some point in July, and when he leaves, Mr. Grant Niemann will take over as lead counsel. Because Mr. Ostberg is away we thought it would be a fine time for Mr. Niemann to come in and at least until Mr. Ostberg returns sit in. So I am pleased this morning to present to your Honours Mr. Grant Niemann here. I am Teresa McHenry. Mr. Turone, Giuliano Turone is co-counsel. Mr. Stefan Waespi, legal adviser with respect to certain matters at issue here, and Ms. Elles van Dusschoten, case manager. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Welcome, Grant, to Celebici. Can we hear the defence? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Good morning, your Honours. My name is Edina Residovic, defence counsel for Mr. Zejnil Delalic. With me in the defence team is my colleague, Eugene O'Sullivan, Professor from Canada.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. MR. OLUJIC (in interpretation): Good morning, your Honours. My name is Zeljko Olujic, attorney from Zagreb. With me as co-defendant (sic) is Mr. Michael Greaves. Together we are defending Mr. Pavo Mucic, the second accused in this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. KARABDIC (in interpretation): Good morning, your Honours. My name is Salih Karabdic, attorney from Sarajevo, defence counsel for Mr. Hazim Delic. With me in the team is Mr. Thomas Moran, attorney from Houston, Texas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Karabdic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours. I'm John Ackerman. I represent Esad Landzo. With me is Cynthia McMurrey as co-counsel representing Mr. Landzo. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we are still on the cross-examination of the last witness, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are still in examination-in-chief of Mr. Moerbauer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Examination-in-chief. It is taking quite a long time doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If your Honours will indulge me for just a moment, you'll recall on Thursday that I pointed out to the court that a couple of volumes of documents that had been delivered by the Prosecutor were unable to be found. They were very quickly located after I made that announcement. I want to make it very clear for the record of this matter that at the time I rose to discuss that, I was trying to let the court know that there may be some problem with access to those documents for all defence counsel because of the fact that they were missing. I did not intend at any point in those remarks to suggest that the Registrar of this Tribunal had in any way failed in terms of security and protection of the defence chambers. To the extent that it was heard in that light, I want to apologise to the Registrar for those remarks. I had no intention of implicating the Registrar in that matter in any way at all, but only to point out to the court that there may be a problem with us accessing the documents for purposes of cross-examination of the witness. So to the extent that the Registrar became concerned about that matter, I had no intention of getting the Registrar involved, and certainly apologise to the Registrar if anybody in this courtroom or outside this courtroom saw it as any kind of a complaint about the kind of job the Registrar does for this Tribunal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ackerman, for your position. I think nobody really ought to have thought that you were inferring any misconduct or careless handling of the security. I know it was understood perhaps something must have gone amiss somewhere. I did not understand it as such. I know many others did not. Can we have the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas Moerbauer (continued)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Remind him he is still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I remind you, Mr. Moerbauer, that you are still under oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (In interpretation): Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, your Honour. We didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Whether the interpreter is sworn ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: She's a different lady.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let her take the oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: She has to take an oath that she will translate correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let her swear the oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I proceed, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, going back to the afternoon of March 18th, 1996, you said that your colleague, Navrat, brought into Room 331 the materials seized in the premises of the firm INDA-BAU right after the house search; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Not translated).

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness will have to repeat. His microphone was not on, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Navrat on 18th March in the afternoon brought the objects to me in Room 331 of police headquarters in Vienna.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You said that among the seized material brought by Mr. Navrat there were about 50 videotapes, which were later classified by your colleague Panzer and watched by you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were around fifty videotapes and Panzer numbered them, but only in the coming, the following days, that is to say the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes. Now may I ask the Registrar to show to Mr. Moerbauer the three items, the three videotapes, which has been marked with numbers 114, 115 and 116, please? (Handed to witness) MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, we object to the showing of these exhibits. The witness has just said that the videos were numbered the following days. He cannot identify the origin of these videos.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honours, these videos were classified the following days but they were given anyway to Mr. Moerbauer, so even if we are going to seek leave in order to call Mr. Panzer as a witness, we will like to show anyway the three videotapes to Mr. Moerbauer in order to ask him if he is in a position to recognise them from their external appearance anyway, since he had them in his hands for a relevant period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You are also going to call Mr. Navrat?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We are going to examine them. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): We have already learned that there is a certain difference in the number of videotapes. We don't even know whether these videotapes were there. So on the basis of our previous objections, which were accepted by the Trial Chamber, this witness cannot identify these objects, because he did not participate in the house search and he gained possession of certain tapes the following days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Now I think it's safer for you to wait for the person who actually seized these tapes, so that he can identify the tapes he seized.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. We are going to call Mr. Navrat to testify on that, but we believe that in order to save time and money, we can anyway today show these videos also to Mr. Moerbauer, since the videos -- they are the videos he received, and then examined from Mr. Navrat. So I ask your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: No one puts the cart before the horse. I thought if you really mean to introduce evidence that someone else seized those tapes and handed them to him, I think it's fairer to bring that person first. Unfortunately if you have not brought him here, then you might bring him later.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We believe that anyway Mr. Navrat will be called to testify, but if he is going to testify in the next future, we might be in a position to call back Mr. Moerbauer to ask him whether they -- these videotapes were the ones he had the possibility to watch later on under an order of Mr. Gschwendt. So I would like to ask this question anyway immediately to Mr. Moerbauer in order to find out whether he can identify that these are the videos he received by Mr. Navrat and then examined himself. Am I allowed to anyway ask this question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You can. You can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. So can you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think your undertaking to call the person who seized them still stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Of course we are going to call Mr. Navrat, who seized the videos, and even Mr. Panzer, who classified them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Are there any identifying marks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Clarify your objections, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just identify any marks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Those who were responsible for seizing the tapes, those who gave the tapes to them will be called to give evidence. If you have any difficulties at that stage, you can put your questions to them. So what is now being formally to lay the foundation of how he got these tapes and what he did with them. So for that purpose his evidence will be accepted. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, I objected and I appreciate the decision of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Moerbauer, are you in a position to recognise these three videos only from the -- from their external appearance and the stickers or labels which appear on them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you look at them and tell them -- what can you say about them and how do you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of the numbering system. This was taken from INDA-BAU at Koppstrasse 22. These videos were given to me by Navrat in the office, in police headquarters, and this is on the cover and on the tape itself, and that's the numbering system that's put on there by Panzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Moerbauer. Mr. Moerbauer, you say that among the seized material brought by Mr. Navrat and given to you by Mr. Navrat and coming from INDA-BAU there were also 12 files?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Which you also later examined thoroughly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Before going ahead, I would like to be sure did the Registrar show him the three videos or only one? Only one. I'm sorry. All three videotapes have to be shown to him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This video as well, numbered I25, was given me by Navrat and Panzer put the stickers on it, the I25. They're both on the case and on the videotape itself. This would have come from INDA-BAU at Koppstrasse 14. Now this videotape has our numbering system on it, I46. That's both the case and the videotape itself. This videotape was also handed over by Navrat and numbered by Panzer. Now, again Koppstrasse 14 would be the source on the basis of the numbering.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right then. So you already told us about the 12 files which you received from Mr. Navrat, and you also reported to us that while you were still in Taubergasse you received from your colleague Unger and Winkelmann material seized in Delalic's apartment, which was later also examined by you in detail; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you receive this material from Mr. Unger or Mr. Winkelmann?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I received the objects from Taubergasse 15/14, the objects seized there at the door. At the end of the search, Taubergasse 15, Door 14, I was given a black sports bag by Unger and the record of the search and the keys to the apartment, which I then handed over to Mr.s Delalic, the keys.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You received that in the very apartment of Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was at the door, in front of the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So at this point may I ask the Registrar to hand over again the binders of the original documents to Mr. Moerbauer? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, I object to the showing of these documents to the witness. The witness did not take part in the search of the apartment. The witness according to his own testimony received a sports bag and not any documents. According to his own testimony it was only from 22nd March-2nd April that the witness examined some papers. There is no basis for him to recognise these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Turone, can you react to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Mr. Moerbauer can identify the documents that he received from other people immediately inside the headquarters of the police. He can -- he is actually the only person who, pursuant to a specific order of the chief of the unit, could examine thoroughly all the seized documents. So he's the person who can identify one by one the documents which he received either from Mr. Unger or from Mr. Navrat, and the documents which were examined by him pursuant to the order of Mr. Gschwendt. There is -- your Honours have indicated already that they wish to hear from the several officers who actually seized the material and then gave it to Mr. Moerbauer, but we are going to do that, but it's still the case, however, that in addition this witness be allowed to recognise every single document he might have received from Unger, either Unger or Navrat, because he is the only person who did a specific detailed inventory of those documents. So I repeat we will call Mr. Navrat, we will call Mr. Unger, but -- we might even call back Mr. Moerbauer after that in order to recognise at that time one by one the documents he received from Mr. Navrat and from Mr. Unger, but in order to save time and money, I think we might ask this witness immediately to go through the documents and see whether he can recognise documents which he received either from Mr. Unger or from Mr. Navrat that same day, March 18th, 1996. So may I be allowed to ask the -- the argument is the same which applies to the three videotapes we just have been showing to this witness. Only Mr. Moerbauer can identify these documents. We will call the other officers to say that they seized certain material and then gave it to Mr. Moerbauer, but we anyway need Mr. Moerbauer to say he received certain material from other officers and he did already, that he reviewed it, reviewed this material carefully, and that he can now identify and recognising documents one by one, since he was the only person who did a detailed inventory of this seized material. On the other hand, there's no real rule that chain evidence must be given in any specific order, so there is nothing wrong --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Please, please, let's not waste so much time. You have said so much things about a simple fact. I thought that since our last sitting it would have occurred to you that the normal and better procedure was to call those people first. Possibly you have difficulties in doing that. Admit that and not argue that there is no order in which a thing should be called in a tidier way. Now these documents or the tapes were not brought from the air. They are related to certain places and in respect of this trial. So you don't just call anybody who got the documents or tapes after several things have happened to state that he got the tapes. The normal link was to have called those who took these tapes or the documents were the place where it is contested it was taken, but for purposes of facilitating the trial, I think since you have undertaken to call these witnesses, we would allow it to be given. That evidence can now be given, provided, of course, you can only tender it when the people who brought it from Delalic's house can show that they got the tapes from that house. Unless you did that, it will not be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This is exactly what we intend to do, your Honour. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, may I be allowed to make an explanation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can make an explanation, but you are delaying the matter, because we definitely would allow this witness to say that he dealt with it on the undertaking that those who handed the tapes to him would come to say so, and then that would be the proper link for how he got it. Yes, you can. You can say what ... MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, I am keen on the expediency of these proceedings, but justice comes first, and I appeal to you, your Honours, to remember that on Thursday when an attempt was made to show this witness a document numbered 10, a handwritten document, you ruled that this witness could not be a witness who could confirm those documents. I, therefore, appeal to you, your Honours, to reconsider our objection, because the witness was not present, he did not receive any papers. He received a sports bag and he gained possession of those papers from 22nd March-2nd April. Therefore, it is a waste of time for this witness to try to identify objects taken from the apartment in which Mr. Delalic resided. I appeal to you, therefore, to taking into account these arguments, to make a final Ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will take them into account when we will decide whether it's admissible or not. All these factors will be taken into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. I want to make clear our intention is not to tender for admission all these documents today but only after at appropriate police officers from Vienna will have testified as proper. So may I ask you, Mr. Moerbauer, since you could examine thoroughly the documents you received either from Mr. Unger or from Mr. Navrat, I'll ask you to look one by one at the documents contained in these two binders in front of you, starting from the document marked with number 113, which is the 10th document on -- my question for every single document is the same. So do you recognise this document as one of the documents originally contained either in the material you received in Delalic's apartment from Mr. Unger or in any of the 12 files you received from Mr. Navrat at the police headquarters, and -- MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's -- MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honour, this is the document on which you ruled on Thursday that it could not be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I say that the objection you raised last week was slightly different, because the question was probably put to the witness in an improper way. Now the question is not whether he can identify this document for having taken part in the search, in the relative search. Now the question is whether he can recognise, identify a document as one of the documents he received from a colleague of his in the very day of March 18th. So this is why the question is now different and the recent Ruling of the Chamber in my opinion allows the witness to answer to the question so formulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, I don't think he's attempting -- Prosecution is attempting here to say that this is a document taken from the residence of Delalic. He's not saying that. What he's saying is this is a document given to him by a colleague in whichever way he got it, but this he identifies as a document given to him by his colleague. Now his colleague, if he's called as a witness, will now say where he got that document which I gave to this witness. That is what he's trying to do. You can go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. So can you watch this document, which is now marked with number 113, the 10th document in the binder, and say whether you recognise it as a document you received by one of these -- of your colleagues and in which binder, in which file was that originally contained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Actually what you should ask him, the documents which he recovered from the sports bag and the documents which he received from Mr. Navrat separately, so that Mr. Navrat, when he comes, he says: "Yes, these are the documents which I recovered" and Mr. Unger --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you receive this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Another important thing. When he received the sports bag and he received the documents from INDA-BAU, did they remain all the time in his custody before he started his examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: That was a question we already put in the last hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Okay. That's all right. I thought I would bring this to your notice.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was in the sports bag which was handed to me from Taubergasse 15, Door 10, by Unger, and in the analysis this document was located in binder with the number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you go ahead to the next document? Skip the next documents, which are transcripts of videos, and go to the document -- I'll tell you -- marked as 117 and say if you recognise it as a document you received from Mr. Navrat and in which of the 12 files was it originally contained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I made an index myself of the seized items and here I can locate the exact binder. Am I allowed to use this index?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE

utterances.text: This document was in binder I4 and was also amongst the items that were handed to me by colleague Navrat following the search at Koppstrasse 14. These were handed to me at Vienna police headquarters.

utterances.text: Let's go then to document 140, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was located in binder I8 and was handed to me by my colleague Navrat at Vienna police headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's now go to document 141, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was located in binder I8 and was handed to me by my colleague Navrat at Vienna police headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's now go to the document marked as 142, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we make some progress in what you're doing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How many more documents have you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We're almost at the end of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I see. I thought you could give him the numbers and he could check and then say all in one sentence: "These documents were handed to me".

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, your Honour, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was located in binder I10 and was handed to me by my colleague Navrat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go then to document 143, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was in binder I10 and was handed to me by my colleague Navrat at Vienna police headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What about document numbered as 144?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was in binder I11 and was handed to me by my colleague Navrat at Vienna police headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go to document 145, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was in binder I11 and was handed to me by my colleague Navrat at Vienna police headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Go, please, to document 146.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was located in binder I11 and was also handed to me by my colleague Navrat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go now to see the group, small group of documents marked by the Registrar as 147 A, B, C. What can you say about those documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These documents were located in binder I11, and these documents -- copies were made of these documents for the Tribunal on 18th March 1996, and these documents -- only copies of these documents were found in police files, were located in police files.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you explain in detail the incident which occurred about these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After on 18th March copies had been made for the people in the Tribunal, then for each document I went and made two copies. So for those documents I made two copies, one for the people from the Tribunal and one for the police administration. A mistake must have been made in that an original must have been handed over to the people of the Tribunal as a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. So this is the end --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What do you suggest in respect of that last document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What is your suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Our intention is to call one of our investigators as a witness on this incident, which took place on March 18th in the police headquarters in Vienna, and ask him about this handing over not only of the copies of these three documents but for a mistake also of the originals. So the originals arrived in advance to this Tribunal, and we'll clarify that with the testimony of the investigator who received both copies and originals of these three last documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Then why is he giving evidence of them when, in fact, he did not deal with the originals himself?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Actually he saw in his office only the photocopies of these documents, because when he photocopied the documents for the Tribunal, for the ICTY, he did two copies, he said, one for the Tribunal and one for his own files. So he found only the photocopies and not the originals any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: So he could not have said anything about the original, since he never saw it at any stage. A.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, he saw the originals, because he was the person who photocopied from the originals for the ICTY, and the real mistake was the handing over of the originals together with the copies of these three documents, but this might be clarified when the investigator of this Tribunal will come and say what happened exactly. Of course, we're not insisting or claiming that we might prove everything concerning these three documents through this witness, but this witness can say what he said about these documents and we wanted him to say what he knew about these documents and, of course, his statement will be assessed together with the statement of the investigator, and your Honours will assess whether that is or is not enough in order to the future admissibility of these documents. I repeat that we are not going to tender any of these documents until all the appropriate witnesses will have testified on those. So the last document which is contained in the binder, Mr. Moerbauer, is marked as 148, and this is nothing to do with the seizures. Could you please say whether you can identify this document 148?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is the record, the Niederschrift. This is on the basis of the questioning on 18th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you recognise your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now I am at the end of my examination-in-chief, but before that I would like to mark for identification the original search record concerning the house search which was handled directly by this witness in the apartment of Mr. Mucic. May I ask -- this Niederschrift, this search record, already made available to the defence lawyers, but we have further copies for them if they wish, and we have copies, of course, for your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What is this document? I'm not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The search record, the search record itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Of?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Of the house search which Mr. Moerbauer took part in personally. So the search carried on in the apartment of Mr. Mucic in Taubergasse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is the record prepared?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The protocol and record prepared and signed by Mucic on the spot of the house search concerning the apartment of Mr. Mucic. This is the house search in which Mr. Moerbauer was present and was one of the officers who carried on the house search. I beg your pardon. Maybe the confusion is done because the word "Niederschrift" in German means record generally. I'm not speaking about the record of the interview, the police interview of Mr. Mucic. I'm talking about the record of the house search done in the apartment of Mr. Mucic. So I would like you, Mr. Moerbauer, to tell us: do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document is the Niederschrift, the record that is drawn up in connection with a search, and it tells you about the search and about the objects seized.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Which search exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the search in the apartment of Zdravko Mucic, Vienna 17, Taubergasse 15, Door 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you say which signatures appear on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Borlak, Panzer, Bycek, Moerbauer are the officers who signed this, and then this document bears the signature of Zdravko Mucic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There is an English translation of this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The English translation will be prepared as soon as possible of course, your Honour. Do you recognise your own signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those are my initials there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm at the end of my examination-in-chief. I would say that my intention is after this testimony to tender for admission only four documents, the two passports and the two ID cards which were seized by this witness in the apartment of Mr. Mucic, and we tender -- we'll tender for admission also the record of the police interview of Mucic dated 18th March 1996 as well as the search record concerning his own apartment. Anyway, we accept -- we do not object to do all this after the end of all the cross-examinations of this witness. We postpone the tendering of any other item after the testimonies of other appropriate witnesses, officers of the Vienna police and also our investigator concerning the last three documents, for which the Prosecution will seek leave to insert their names in the witness list. Concerning the very first document, the one marked as 104, our inclination is to consider it only an aide memoire for the witness and we're not going to tender it as evidence anyway. So this is the end of the examination-in-chief and the videos also will be tendered after Mr. Panzer will have and Mr. Navrat will have testified. So right now the tendering for admission will deal with four documents seized in Mucic's apartment, the interview of Mucic and the search record I would say after cross-examinations will be over, if your Honours deem that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You are not tendering that information which was given. We were told by Mr. Gschwendt that the document is given to the person detained containing his rights. Are you not tendering that in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We tendered that already together with the testimony of Mr. Gschwendt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so I'm clear on this, as I understand it the Prosecution is not now and has no intention of ever introducing Prosecution Exhibit 104; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Our original intention was to tender exhibit 104 as exhibit for admission, but let us say we do not feel so strong about that. We could also consider that simply as an aide-memoire this witness used for testifying unless, of course, defence lawyers would -- should appreciate that document and your Honours should think it is useful as evidence. In that case we would be happy to go back to our original intention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has left that to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: The reason I ask that, your Honour, is that thing is full of references to documents that we've never seen, are not any part of the record of this case. It has got analysis in the thing: "This means that. Something else means something else". To me it is something that if they are not going to introduce it into evidence, I don't know why it's in the record and I would like it removed from the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I support what Mr. Moran says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Is it part of the record now? As what?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It has been described as an aide-memoire. An aide memoire can't be evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: It can be if it is tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If he is using it as an aide-memoire, it is simply refreshing his memory. That is not, my submission, a piece of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He's not insisting on it. He said he left it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Well, we object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Judge, I don't think the thing ought to be anywhere around. I don't think it ought to be in my notebook, your notebook. Presumably the Registrar will keep a copy just to prove it was here at some point in time, but it's just something that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We'll not look at it if it's not part of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I appreciate that, judge. I know that you won't. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I should like to join my colleagues in their objections. I should also like to object to the tendered documents of two passports and two ID cards being admitted because, according to the testimony of this witness, he was not present in the apartment of Mr. Mucic throughout the search.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: He has not tendered them yet, has he? He hasn't. He's merely telling you he would wish to. Until it is tendered and received, we could not regard it as anything valid here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now rise and resume at 12 o'clock for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Would you kindly invite the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Please remind the witness that he is still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, I remind you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Any cross-examination for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. The cross-examination will proceed in this way: first, counsel for Mr. Delalic; second, counsel for Mr. Delic; third, counsel for Mr. Landzo; and, fourth, counsel for Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Good day, your Honours. May I begin?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you. Good day, Mr. Moerbauer. My name is Edina Residovic. I'm defence counsel for Mr. Delalic. I apologise. I have some technical problems. Mr. Moerbauer, you confirmed, testifying before this court, that you were an officer of the Austrian police; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, you are working in the federal administration in Vienna in the Department for State Security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the division for the Protection of the State and for the Protection of Peoples and Property.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have been an inspector since 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since 1992 I have been a District Inspector.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of your training in addition to subjects linked directly to policing, you also studied certain legal subjects; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you were particularly familiar with the provisions of the law on criminal procedure of Austria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do know these provisions for my activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually you are applying the provisions of that law in practice all the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your career you had many cases of arrest of suspects?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also had many cases of house searches and searches of other premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also had many cases of temporary seizure of objects?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have also been trained for monitoring people and collecting information about people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the case of arrest, seizure and search you are obliged to strictly follow the instructions of the court; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have also sought in the course of your career to follow the instructions of the court and to abide by the provisions of the Austrian law; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that in the case of unlawful procedure, the evidence you collect would not be admissible to the court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, would you agree with me if I say that Vienna is an open European city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that there are more than 100,000 foreigners living in it today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that considering the work you do, you were often in contact with foreigners, including when criminal proceedings were being brought against them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this connection you also had communications with Interpol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in this case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, can you confirm that even before the war in the territory of former Yugoslavia, in Austria and more particularly in Vienna, a large number of people from the territory of the former Yugoslavia were living and working in Vienna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in the course of the war in the territory of former Yugoslavia a certain change occurred in the composition of people from the territory of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that can be said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that before the war most of the people from the former Yugoslavia were of Serbian ethnic origin and during the war the number of people from Bosnia and Herzegovina increased?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the majority of the population in Vienna were citizens from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and, secondly, were Bosnians and, third, Croatians, people of Croatian ethnic origin.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Moerbauer, would you agree with me if I said that it has been alleged that the Austrian police is among the most capable in Europe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't pass judgment on this, because I don't know exactly how other police forces work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I thought you would agree. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): In any event, you can confirm that your police is seeking to protect the neutrality of Austria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that Vienna is the headquarters of a certain number of international organisations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that for that reason the Austrian police are equipped with significant technical facilities to be able to perform their duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We have the technical facilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You personally are working in the headquarters of the Austrian Federal Police, which is in the centre of Vienna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this headquarters is also equipped with considerable technical facilities for the taking of statements, for copying, recording, re-recording and the like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not correct. If you take video equipment, for example, we don't have the possibility, for example, to record, to make video recordings of questionings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I can't hear again. Could you please repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Concerning -- if you're talking about video equipment for the video recording of questionings, then I can't agree with you. We don't have a video camera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have video equipment for re-recording?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we do have this equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also have photocopying machinery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Moerbauer, you participated in the police operation that was conducted at the request of the prosecution of the International Tribunal in connection with the arrest of Mr. Mucic, the search of the apartment and business premises, and temporary confiscation of objects which allegedly belonged to Mr. Zejnil Delalic and to Mr. Zdravko Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The administrative procedure, this was carried out following an order, a court order, which followed an extradition procedure from the International Tribunal and from the Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could somebody help us, please? We cannot hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we get any of the engineers to come and look at it? (Pause). You can now carry on, I think. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Yes, thank you. It's fine now, your Honours. Mr. Moerbauer, I should like to ask you to be kind enough to answer my question once again. Did you participate in this police operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did participate in this operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Austrian police prepared this operation well; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were linked to your colleagues in Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not personally in contact.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you know that such a contact existed; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that this was the first operation of its kind, as you said, to act according to the law was essential?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that the operation of house searches at all the localities was carried out simultaneously; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was planned as such.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is why you first took some information about the premises that you were going to search?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also carried out the identification of persons residing in those premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And so you established that in Taubergasse number 15, apartment number 10, was occupied by Mr. Zdravko Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also established that in the apartment of MAS, Taubergasse 15, apartment number 14, was occasionally occupied by Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zejnil Delalic was registered at this address until November of the previous year, but we're not able to ascertain whether he was still residing there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you also establish that on the ground floor was the BH Society, of this same building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this was also ascertained.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also established that Rizvanovic Sefika, the sister of Mr. Zejnil Delalic, was also residing at this address?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sefika Delalic (sic) was registered at Taubergasse 15, Door 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also established that at this address at the same entrance Harija Delalic, Mr. Delalic's sister-in-law, was residing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, Harieta (sic) Delalic was registered at Taubergasse 15, but I don't know what apartment exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All the information you have now confirmed was conveyed by you to the court when you asked for a search warrant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not me who obtained the search warrant. It was from Department 210, and this was a result of a previous procedure and the knowledge was transmitted from Department 210 to the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask you, Mr. Moerbauer, if you could, to look at these documents which have been submitted to the court and to try and identify them. I beg the assistance of the Registry so that the documents may be shown to the witness and the Prosecution. (Handed to Prosecution).

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: May we just ask defence counsel if there are English translations? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I do not have English translations. I should like the witness to see them because they are in his native tongue. (Handed to witness). Mr. Moerbauer, is this document indicating that on 15th March 1996, with this date -- the document with this date, was this document the document that was sent to the judge, Dr Seda, the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document contains -- belongs to a preliminary procedure. It's part of a preliminary procedure and this was not produced for this particular case. It was for notification of this case. This notification is annexed to a report, which is also in the court proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell me whether this is a document which says in the heading "Zahl: 1 313 168/1-II/10/K 1", the first document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I know is that part -- well, with regard to this registration information, this is part of the court file.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I read out well the number of the first page that I gave to you and the date, 15th March 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The reference there, that's from Division 210. Now, the first page of this document was not drawn up by our department, but the following four pages I do recognise. That is the registration information I put together. I do recognise that, and this was provided in another connection, and for purposes of information it was passed on to Magister Gross to Department 210. It is on that basis that the court went ahead and issued the search warrant.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely what I'm asking, Mr. Moerbauer. On the first page, which was not issued by your department, the last sentence, does it ask the court to issue search warrants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I do not know when the facts of Magister Gross went to Dr Seda. This is the first time I've seen this. All I can tell you is that I'm familiar with the annex.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, you have just said that you recognise the next four pages. Could you tell me whether this is information about all the tenants who were to be found at the address Taubergasse number 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This registration information includes the following people, who at one point in time were living -- were registered as living there or de-registered as living at that building in Taubergasse 15. This stems from the police station of the 17th District in Vienna.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that this list contains more than ten persons of age?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on this list we find also the name of Rizvanovic Sefika, the sister of Mr. Zejnil Delalic, as the tenant at number 15, apartment number 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Moerbauer, you said that at the beginning of March you met with representatives of Interpol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before that meeting you personally were not aware, nor did you have information to show that with respect to Mr. Zejnil Delalic there was an extradition request on the part of an international organisation or any other country, Yugoslavia, Bosnia-Herzegovina or Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Previous to the get-together with the people from Department 210 Panzer did make known to me on 6th March, as far as I can recall, there had been some contacts about the request for extradition concerning Zdravko Mucic, and the get-together with the people from 210 was brought to my attention only later. Well, it only occurred later, and that's when details were discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, but I asked you then before that you were not aware at all of any requests with respect to Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prior to 6th March, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, you stated that you arrested Mr. Zdravko Mucic on 18th March 1996 at 14:15 hours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that after the arrest during the following fifteen minutes you went to his apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you would agree with me if I say that you entered Mr. Mucic's apartment at 14:30 hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, between 2.15 and 2.30 in the afternoon. That would have been the latest time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Moerbauer, enter together with Mr. Mucic -- did you enter his apartment together with Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we all entered the apartment together.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that at that moment there was no one in the apartment and that his daughter, Sanda, came a little later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, Sanda Mucic was already in the apartment. She may have come from the neighbouring apartment to the apartment door, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But the moment you entered, she was not in the apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember that precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you, Mr. Moerbauer, remember which are the persons who entered Mr. Mucic's apartment together with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Borlak, Bycek and Panzer, those officers?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When Sanda Mucic entered the apartment you asked her to interpret your conversation with Mr. Mucic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Sanda Mucic was in the apartment and explained -- well, we told her to explain to her father because he didn't understand all that well. It was a bit of excitement and apparently he lost his knowledge of German at that moment. For the purpose of the arrest we asked Sanda to explain matters to him, explain the search, and this took place just at the entrance, the little hallway within the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that moment you knew that Sanda Mucic was a minor and that she was only 16?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't note that fact, because I didn't go into any details about Sanda Mucic, but on the basis of her experience -- her appearance, one could readily take her for 18 or 19 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, you just confirmed that a report on the tenants of Taubergasse 15 contains your -- the information you collected about the tenants of that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This report -- but this registration information was not put together in connection with this operation. This has to do with a different matter and it wasn't wholly up-to-date, in fact. Now, these are the apartments --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, you confirmed this information as being yours. On page 2 it says that Sanda Mucic was born in 1979. Is that correct, that that is what is written there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is what's in the registration information, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You just said, Mr. Moerbauer, that there was a bit of excitement and that Mr. Mucic may have forgotten the language that you assumed he spoke; is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when we did our previous enquiries, we found that Mucic had been questioned back in 1991 and that the questioning proceeded without an interpreter, and this was also on the basis of a court order that we went ahead with the record of that interview, and we took it that Mucic was acquainted with the German language, and when he was under -- when we contacted him in the course of our investigations on the 14th, we did find that he did know some German.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, probably Mr. Mucic does speak some German, but you said that he was excited. I would like to know whether at the moment when Sanda Mucic entered the apartment and saw her father being arrested was she, too, extremely excited or upset, being a child?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in fact, she dealt with it quite well, and a child -- she was older than 14 so she was not a child according to our legal system.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, do you speak foreign languages and can you assess to what extent somebody speaks a foreign language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I speak bad English and my knowledge of English must be about equivalent to Mucic's knowledge of German. I'd say we're on a par.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you don't speak Serbo-Croatian or Croato-Serbian at all or, as it is nowadays more modern to describe it as, Bosnian-Serbian-Croatian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you cannot assess at all whether a person is interpreting correctly from these languages into German and vice versa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't have that possibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, was Sanda Mucic present throughout and did she interpret everything that was necessary for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was present when Mr. Mucic was informed of the grounds for the arrest and of the grounds of the search. She was present there and she was also present during part of the search.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore Sanda Mucic was present throughout the search of the apartment in their apartment, which is in Taubergasse 15, Apartment 10?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as to whether she was there the whole time I can't recall but at times -- at any event she was present at the beginning when we began the search.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, was Sanda Mucic the only person to interpret to Zdravko Mucic what you wanted to convey to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Harija Delalic and Anela Lizlic (si) were in the apartment for a short period of time as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore you saw Harija Delalic in Mr. Mucic's apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. She was near the entrance. The door was ajar, the apartment door and in the entrance hall there were those two women, Harija Delalic and the other woman I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, was Sanda Mucic present during the search carried out in the MAS company, which was situated at number 28?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Moerbauer. Let me ask you things that you are aware of. A moment ago you said that roughly around 2.30pm the search started of Mr. Zdravko Mucic's apartment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On Thursday you stated that that search lasted about 45 minutes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Now with regard to the exact times involved, you can see what they are in the records, in the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If it is correct that the search lasted 45 minutes, one could roughly say that the search in Mr. Mucic's apartment ended at 15:15; is that roughly correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The search I can't say if we put down the time at which it was over, that is to say when we locked the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The notes you made about the search are to be found in the minutes made on the spot, which you call Niederschrift; is that correct, Niederschrift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Niederschrift, the record began -- we started taking that down in Mucic's apartment, and then we finished it at police headquarters, but only in this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But I'm asking you, Mr. Moerbauer, whether we are talking about the Niederschrift in which, as you say, you indicate the time when the search of a certain premises has been completed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the Niederschrift you have the time when the search was over or the time at which the apartment was locked. I can't tell you precisely which of those two times was indicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Moerbauer. Please did you take part in the search of the BH Society?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was involved in that search as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, we are due for lunch now. We can break for lunch. We will continue after the lunch break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Can we have the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, I think it is you still cross-examining. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. Mr. Moerbauer, we could continue; right? I think that the last question I had for you was whether on that day, 18th March 1996, a search of the BH Club was conducted simultaneously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The search of the BH Club was not carried out at exactly the same time. It was carried out by colleagues Bycek, or there were three colleagues who were present. Mr. Panzer was also there and myself and at this time the search of his apartment ended and we began the search at the BH Club.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you were in the BH Club during the search as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was also present during the search of this club.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also present there as a witness was also Djemal Delalic, who is the club secretary; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that Djemal Delalic was present during this search.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time during the search you knew that Djemal Delalic was the brother of Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Panzer was also aware of that, Mr. Panzer who, as you said, was in charge of this police operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He also knew that this was the brother of Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, on that day a search was also conducted of the MAS company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Zdravko Mucic was also present at this search in the MAS company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zdravko Mucic was not present during the search, that is Taubergasse 28, the MAS company.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You had regularly issued warrants for all these searches; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had search warrants in two versions. The first warrant, search warrant, was for four addresses or five addresses, because Taubergasse 14 and Taubergasse 16 were given. These search warrants were not quite up-to-date, that is the premises where they should be carried out were not quite updated, so there was a proposal made to the court for these search warrants, so a second search warrant was issued where the premises were given more accurately. This was done by the court. So Taubergasse 15, Door 10, and Taubergasse 15 and 15 were not given accurately on the first search warrant and the --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would maybe prefer you to give me shorter answers, even though I appreciate some of the longer ones that you have given me. I am going to give you this other warrant, so if I can have the usher to please show this to the Prosecution first and then pass it on to the witness. Thank you. (Handed to Prosecution). (Handed to witness). Mr. Moerbauer, is this the warrant that you have just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's the last search warrant that we received from the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, did you serve the search warrant on Mr. Delalic on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, Zejnil Delalic or Djemal Delalic? Which?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zejnil Delalic could not be served this warrant, because he was not in Vienna.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He was not served this warrant within the following 24 hours either; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this warrant has not been served on him until the present day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He has still not yet been served this warrant. The police did not serve this warrant on Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at the bottom of page 1 of this document, of this police warrant, it says that you had to serve it immediately or within the next 24 hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is corrected -- this is correct, and this was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the line seven from the top on this page of the document, and if you can find where it says that the items that refer to the war crimes in Bosnia and especially the prisoner torture videotapes are to be examined. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, I would like to confirm whether I understood well what you said in the direct examination. Is it correct that you -- that on March 18th at the address of Taubergasse 15 as well as other premises you started the search warrants that are quoted in the warrants issued by the Tribunal at roughly the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More or less, yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand correctly, Mr. Moerbauer, that you stated that you, together with Mr. Mucic and your colleagues, whom you have also mentioned today, as well as Sanda Mucic, entered the apartment of Mr. Mucic, where you conducted the search?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you at that time did not go to the second floor where the search of the apartment where Mr. Delalic was staying was also to be conducted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shortly -- at Door 10, when the search was finished in Zdravko Mucic's apartment at Door 10, then the search was carried out at the MAS company. I was very shortly -- I spent a short amount of time at Door 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, sir, if you could just answer this question now, and then that question will follow. In other words, at the time when you entered the apartment of Mr. Mucic your colleagues Unger and Winkelman went to the second floor to search the apartment of Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were not present at the time when they entered the apartment of Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not present at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, is it true that you stated that much later in the apartment of Mr. Mucic, where you were at that time with Mr. Mucic and Sanda Mucic and two other colleagues of yours, another colleague came down, a colleague that had been searching the apartment of Mr. Delalic, and he informed you that in that apartment several documents were found that -- regarding the former Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that point you climbed up to the apartment of Zejnil Delalic and on a table you saw a number of videotapes and documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that none of this material was marked in any way; it was all in one heap?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is also correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that time you said: "Fine. Let's take all these documents along", and then you returned to the apartment of Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that time the search in the apartment of Mr. Mucic was not completed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that point in time the search had already finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Moerbauer. In the heap of materials that you saw did you recognise items that regard the war -- materials relating to the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina and to the torture of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw some files. I also saw certificates, and they were signed by a commander or they were for military purposes, or for military activities, but I couldn't establish this exactly, because it was in the Serbo-Croatian language.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you did not have an interpreter along with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no interpreter present during the search.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not order your colleagues to put together a precisely drawn document with the items that were outside of the court order?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour. Your interpreter has not quite understood that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly repeat that. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Did you instruct your colleagues to make a separate record of all the items that did not concern the war crimes in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the torture of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not indicate this specifically here to the colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also did not draw attention to your colleague that this separate list should be forwarded directly to the public prosecutor of Austria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Colleagues had the search warrant and knew what it was about and I did not give the colleagues any particular indications. It was just a question of whether they should seize the videotapes and the documents, and I indicated that this should be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you entered the apartment of Mr. Delalic you only had contact with your colleagues Unger and Winkelman in that premises; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only had contact with these two persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time in the apartment of Mr. Delalic there were no third persons present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see any third person.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, a short while ago we discussed Sanda Mucic, and she's an underage person. Please can you tell me whether you know that Sanda Mucic and her brother, who is also very young, that both of them lived only with their father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Moerbauer, that at one point while you were in the apartment of Mr. Mucic a proposition was made that Sanda Mucic, as an underage person, would be taken and turned over to the appropriate authorities of the social care services?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Harija Delalic was also in the apartment and in the questioning with Zdravko Mucic this problem was also discussed, and we were aware that the mother was also present in Vienna and that the children could be left in the apartment and Harija Delalic would be requested by Mr. Mucic to take care of the -- future care of the children.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will request now that you answer the following questions in a very short way. So during the search of the apartment of Zdravko Mucic the question was raised where to put up Sanda Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was discussed at the end of the search.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This question was resolved in such a way that Ms. Harija Delalic took on the obligation to take care of Sanda Mucic; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the provisional solution, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This took place in the apartment of Mr. Zdravko Mucic; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this occurred in the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also saw Harija Delalic later, when you gave her the keys to the apartment where Mr. Zejnil Delalic used to live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not see Harija Delalic on other occasions on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's possible that she was in the apartment of Delalic or in front of the apartment of Delalic the first time at least. Harija Delalic was in Mucic's apartment as well and it's also possible that she spent a short time in the apartment above.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, do you recall that when asked by me you answered that at the time when you were conducting this search warrant in Mr. Mucic's place that Harija Delalic was in front of the apartment of Mr. Mucic together with another person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that Ms. Delalic was in the front room or was in the doorway.
