utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You do not speak the truth before this Trial Chamber a short while ago when asked by me you said when entering of Mr. Delalic's apartment no third person was present beside your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I noticed Harija Delalic in the apartment above. I don't know exactly when, but I can't answer the question with 100 per cent accuracy as to whether she was in the apartment or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you are not sure where you saw Harija Delalic on the second floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether she was inside the apartment or in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At that moment, Mr. Moerbauer, did you know that Harija Delalic was the wife of the deceased brothers of Mr. Zejnil Delalic, in other words, she was a sister-in-law of Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was aware of this. Harija Delalic is the widow of Sefik Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, do you know that she lives on the first floor immediately next to the apartment of Mr. Zdravko Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She came out of this apartment but I didn't know exactly whether she lived there or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Moerbauer, could you tell me whether your colleagues informed you that Sevko Rizvanovic, the sister of Mr. Delalic, asked to be present at the search of the apartment of Mr. Delalic and she was removed by your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know anything with regard to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that your colleagues Unger and Winkelman forbade Ms. Razeamedovic, who is an acquaintance of Mr. Delalic, who was accidently in the building at that time, to be present at the search and temporary seizure of items?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know anything with relation to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, you said that your colleagues turned over the items found -- items belonging to Mr. Delalic in front of the apartment and these items were placed in a sports bag; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I got that sports or gym bag at the end of the search, when the apartment was locked.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you received this sports gym bag together with the keys to the apartment of Mr. Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You gave the keys to the apartment of Mr. Delalic to Ms. Harija Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were also given the record, the Niederschrift, right there on the spot; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I got the record as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, was this gym bag that you received outside of the apartment of Mr. Delalic -- was this bag sealed properly and taped properly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The gym bag had a zipper on it so it could be zipped up and it was brought to the vehicle, and then we drove to police headquarters with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But it is correct that it was not sealed and that the zipper was easy to unzip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would have been possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, is it correct that on that day all planned search on the premises in Taubergasse 15 was conducted, that is including the BH Club, the apartment of Mr. Mucic and the apartment in which Mr. Delalic stayed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all three searches were carried out on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on that day, March 18th, the search was also completed at the premises of the MAS company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you know that on this day, March 18th, a search was conducted of the Inda-Bau premises as well and the apartment of Djemal Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Moerbauer, that after this day, March 18th, no additional searches were conducted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, not by our department at any event and in relation to this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, there was no additional search of the apartment where Mr. Delalic stayed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Rea (sic) Delalic, is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I mean additional, later, and I'm referring now to the apartment where Mr. Delalic stayed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our department in this relation did not conduct any further searches.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, I'll now ask you to look at the Niederschrift on the searches conducted so that I can ask some more questions of you. I will ask that this Niederschrift be shown to the Prosecution and then passed on to the witness. (Handed to Prosecution). (Handed to witness). Before the document is given to the witness, I would request that it would be marked for identification. Could we please have it marked, this document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is already on. It's marked as D40/1. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you. Mr. Moerbauer, would you look at the last sentence on this page, where it states: "18th March 1996 at 15:30 hours". Sir, since I don't speak German, could you please confirm that this text means that the search in the above-mentioned apartment -- I'm sorry -- that on the premises in Taubergasse 15 the association Bosnia-Herzegovina in the presence of Djemal Delalic, a search was conducted on March 18th at 15:30 and that the record, the Niederschrift, was given to this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the persons conducting the search are Bycek, Panzer and you, Moerbauer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please read at the top right corner the text that is stated there, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which text are you referring to, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is the first page, the text starting with: "Vienna, ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vienna, that's in 8 or 9. You can't really make it out. There's probably an error there in the wording.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, in that corner it states that this -- it states that the search was conducted on 19th March 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It could be half a 9 or half an 8 what I have here, but this Niederschrift was drawn up on 18th March.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, could you please look at the second record, which is the Niederschrift of the search on the premises of the MAS company? I also -- may I also have it marked for identification and shown to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is marked as D31/1. The transcript said D40/1 for the earlier one, but that is D30/1. (Handed to Prosecution). (Handed to witness).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This Niederschrift, this record --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please at the bottom of this record does it state that the search was completed on 18th March 1996 at 15:15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this record signed by Mr. Zdravko Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was signed by Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the top right corner does it say that the search was conducted on 19th March 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the reason for that is the following. The searches had been scheduled for 19th March and the Niederschriften the records, were prepared. That's also why they're typed. Now those were the things that were hard and fast. Now the handwriting was added on the spot, and that's also why there was this mistake with the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you confirmed that one part of this record was put together beforehand in the police -- at the police station; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is a standard form, and there's things that have to be filled in, so those things that were hard and fast, for example the person concerned, the crime, the grounds for this search, that we knew, so that was entered in there in advance, and the things that might change, the officers involved, the witnesses, the seized objects, etc, that was filled out only on the scene of the search.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, a part of the record with certain information on this form was put together at a different location and much earlier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, is it correct that a record can be signed only by persons who were present at the search?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. There's an exception. When it's signed by the person concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, did you confirm today that Mr. Zdravko Mucic was not present at the search of the premises of the MAS company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you telling the truth at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is true that Mr. Zdravko Mucic did sign this record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, I would like you to look at the record, the Niederschrift, of the apartment of Mr. Mucic together with me, and I would also like to have it marked for identification and shown to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We did already mark this for identification during the examination-in-chief. Maybe you forgot about that, but anyway. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I apologise. Thank you very much. So please if I can show the already marked document of the record of the search of the apartment of Mr. Mucic. Before we move to this record, I would only like to confirm whether I recall correctly your answer that the search of the MAS company was conducted after the search of the apartment of Mr. Zdravko Mucic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please go back to the record of the search of the MAS company premises, please? Is it correct that at the bottom of the first page of this record it states that the search was completed in 15:15 hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like, Mr. Moerbauer, to look at the Niederschrift of the search of the apartment of Mr. Zdravko Mucic, which, as you stated, was conducted between 14:30 and 15:15 hours, that means 45 minutes. Mr. Moerbauer, this is the only record, as you said, which you started writing in the apartment and completed on the premises of the Police Department headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The record, the Niederschrift, of the objects seized, that was done at the police headquarters, and that's also where the signatures were applied.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, I did understand correctly that the search of the apartment of Mr. Mucic was also conducted on 18th March 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please can you tell me what date is stated on the top corner of the first page of this record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 19th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell me at the bottom of the first page what date is stated as the date when this search was completed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 19th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were present at this search?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this record contains some incorrect data regarding the time of the search and the day of the search; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the record it's only the first date, 19th March 1996, and that goes back to the initial error.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the search was completed on the following day, on 19th March. That is stated at the bottom of this record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says that this record was drawn up on the 19th, and after midnight Mucic went into police custody. So this was in the early morning hours of the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, on 18th March -- at midnight on 18th March you did not start putting together, drawing up the record of the items seized in the apartment of Mr. Zdravko Mucic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the record the objects were indicated before midnight. This took place at police headquarters. Now confirmation of that record took place on 19th March 1996 and Mucic was brought into court custody and this Niederschrift was not typed up in advance like the others, and the date there was only added subsequently. It wasn't typed in in advance.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, at the search of the apartment of Mr. Zdravko Mucic in his case no record was made simultaneously at the time of the search?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Niederschrift, the handwritten information about the officials involved, etc, the seized objects, were added subsequently at police headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, I do understand that certain things are obvious to you. What we are trying to determine here is the exact condition of the documents themselves. Mr. Moerbauer, would you please take a look at the Niederschrift, that is the record, drawn up at the spot at the apartment where Mr. Zejnil Delalic stayed and which was at Taubergasse 15/14. Please can I have this document marked for identification, shown to the Prosecution and after that passed on to the witness? Thank you. (Handed to Prosecution). (Handed to witness). Mr. Moerbauer, the search of the apartment of Mr. Zejnil Delalic, as you stated, was conducted by Messrs Unger and Winkelman. You confirmed that the beginning of the search of the apartment was roughly at the same time when you entered the apartment of Mr. Zdravko Mucic with Mr. Panzer and with the daughter of Mr. Mucic, Sanda Mucic; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In this context, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, before this Trial Chamber you also stated that at the time, at the moment when you entered the apartment of Mr. Delalic at the request of one of your colleagues there was no other person present in the apartment beside your colleagues; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Taubergasse 15/14 the first time I was there, whether Harija Delalic was there I don't know exactly. Sanda Mucic -- I did not notice Sanda Mucic there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, could you tell me that in this record it has been noted that in the apartment of Mr. Zejnil Delalic during this search Sanda Mucic was also present, that is the daughter of the -- the 16 year old daughter of Mr. Mucic, Mr. Pavo Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is stated as such in the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also confirmed that the search of Mr. Mucic's apartment lasted until 3.15 and that during that time Sanda Mucic was interpreting everything needed -- that was needed to be said to her father, Mr. Zdravko Mucic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that this search was completed around 3.15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that at the search in the apartment of -- Mr. Zejnil Delalic's apartment was conducted on 18th March and there were no additional searches following that one; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct in the top corner of the first page of the Niederschrift, and the address is Taubergasse 15/10, -- 15/14 in the apartment of Mr. Zejnil Delalic the search was conducted on 19th March 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The date was actually a mistake here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at the bottom of this page of the Niederschrift on the search of the apartment where Mr. Zejnil Delalic stayed, it is also indicated that this search was completed on 19th March 1996 at 4.10?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The form was filled out showing this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you stated that the form was drawn up with the information that was possible to fill out and they were typed up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the information that was already known that didn't change anything as far as the content of the record was concerned, of the Niederschrift, this was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in handwriting the information was added that was only found after the -- you were on the premises; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also true that it is in the ---- in handwriting it is also stated that the search of the apartment of Mr. Delalic was completed on 19th March 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is stated in handwriting that the record was confirmed or was completed on 19th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, the information about the times of the search as written down in this document are not accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, I'm going to ask you to look at the record, the Niederschrift, of the search of the Inda-Bau. Please if I can also have it marked for identification, then shown to the Prosecution and then passed on to the witness. (Handed to Prosecution). (Handed to witness). Mr. Moerbauer, you were not present during this search; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you stated that on every record the time of its completion, that is the sealing of the apartment has to be indicated, and also the time when this record was submitted to the person whose premises are being searched, that is to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's just a form and the times are given for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, is this the only document drawn up on premises in the presence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Apart from the record of Mucic, all records were carried out on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the top corner, does it state that it was conducted on 19th March 1996, even though it was actually conducted on a different day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it occurred on 18th March.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this record does not state at all whether this search was completed, when it was completed and whether this warrant was ever served on the persons who were at the premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This record shows that completion of this record as confirmation did occur without giving any time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me where is the date and the time given as to when this search was completed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The record -- the completion of this record occurred but the time and place was not filled in.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that the search was completed but no other person can glean from this record whether it was completed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These records made on the spot are the basis from which you then turn over these items to other persons who have different duties in the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This record is something in addition. For every search a report is also drawn up.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This record, Mr. Moerbauer, is the basis for all your future reports, and it is the only document which is drawn up in the presence of the owner, that is the witness, and which is left with the owner, that is the witness; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document is confirmation for the person whose place is being searched and is a record of whether items were found and which items were seized.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the witness who confirms that you allegedly found certain items on the premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, could you again look at the record of the search of the Inda-Bau? On page 2 it is stated that 51 video cassettes were exempt, two recorders with newspapers and eight registers with Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in no way the video cassettes or the number or the documents or other characteristics of the documents seized from the Inda-Bau were indicated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (No translation).

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, judge. Your Honour, I think it may be solved. We were not getting a translation in English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises for not switching on his microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The items which are listed on the record were given to me in a box by my colleague Navrat at police headquarters in Vienna, and this box, a note was attached to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That satisfies me as an answer. You already stated, and I would like you to confirm this, that all these items were brought in a cardboard box to the room number 331 in the police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated, and I would like you to confirm it, if you can, that this room is the room where you, Mr. Panzer and Mr. Bycek work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is the room to which Mr. Zdravko Mucic was brought on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the room where four persons from the International Tribunal also came on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that day in that room your superior, Mr. -- and I apologise; I forget his name -- he was also present there. Mr. Gschwendt, Mr. Gschwendt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is also the room where the interpreter for German language was also present, the interpreter that was needed for the interview with Mr. Zdravko Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The interpreter was also present.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, is it correct that you stated during the direct examination that on that day when you saw this cardboard box you only glanced at the things that were brought in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that none of the items in the box were marked either by certain markings or in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only items in the box from the company Inda-Bau were not marked or the individual binders just received an initial for each binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that point in time you could not even guess the number of items and the contents -- their contents of the items in this box?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The number of videotapes was not checked. It was assumed that this -- that what was in the record, in the Niederschrift, was correct as far as the number of videotapes was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And there was no registration of the number of documents at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was not yet any enumeration of the documents at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Moerbauer, that in the same room, number 331, other items found and seized from the apartment of Mr. Mucic and the apartment of Mr. Delalic and the Inda-Bau company were also brought?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I repeat: is it correct if I state that you stated before this Trial Chamber only four video cassettes seized from Mr. Zdravko Mucic were marked and that the marking of other cassettes was conducted in the following days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, in Moerbauer, that the cardboard box brought in by your colleagues from Inda-Bau was not taped or sealed or registered by people who were at the premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The box was open and it was not marked when it was given to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do I recall correctly, Mr. Moerbauer, that you stated before this Trial Chamber that the items in this box were glanced at by the representatives of the International Tribunal and by their interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The binders were looked through concerning the Inda-Bau search and the video cassettes from the Mucic apartment were also viewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I hope he understood your question. Just repeat that question. Kindly repeat that question. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr. Moerbauer, you just very precisely stated that only the cassettes from Mr. Mucic's apartment were viewed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Mucic tapes were given to the people from the Tribunal and the Inda-Bau tapes were not viewed by the people from the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Is it true, Mr. Moerbauer, that you stated that the interpreter gave you somewhere between 30 and 50 documents from the cardboard box from Inda-Bau and requested that they be copied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The interpreter did not take the documents from the box. The interpreter received the binders one by one. She looked through the binders. Individual documents were copied from the binders. The numbers of the binders were taken and the binder was then placed back into the box.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's all right. Let me ask you one thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Residovic, let's go for a break and come back at 4.30. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): That is also my view, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly remind the witness he's still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, may I remind you that you are still under oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, you can continue. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. Before I continue with the cross-examination of the witness, I should like to ask you to hear a comment, namely I do not speak German, and I rely on the interpretation I receive from our interpreters. My client, Mr. Zejnil Delalic, who is a court translator for German, has informed me that the translations of Mr. Moerbauer's statements made up to the break by the interpreter were not correct, that they do not reflect everything the witness says, so that relying on this opinion of his, I should like to ask you if you could request from the translation service that the interpretation of the testimony of this witness should be done by the interpreter who was working this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think as far as we know it's the same interpreter who has been here since this morning. You mean the interpreter in the booth? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): In the booth, yes. All I can do is make a request. I do not know what the possibilities are for providing another interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If he makes an observation of error, then something has to be done to correct the continuance of any errors. I suppose it might be some technical difficulties. If not, I do not see why the same interpreter could not have interpreted to everyone else. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Also having examined the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us see what we can do before you compound the error.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Maybe a solution that the interpreter which is sitting next to Mr. Moerbauer, if she notices that there's a difference in the translation, if she could notice that and indicate that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That will be a double check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: A cross-check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That will be a double check.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And then ask the witness to repeat or what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If you observe that there is any discrepancy in the interpretation, you can then call the attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We will have a double check now. Okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I suppose this might assist. I know it might not be foolproof, but it might improve it. You can now continue. Let's try this out. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. I know that it is difficult to interpret into four languages, and I should like to thank you for taking steps immediately. I, too, have looked through the transcript and I would like to ask Mr. Moerbauer to allow me to repeat a question, because I think that the answer we see in the transcript doesn't quite faithfully reflect the statement of the witness, probably because of the already mentioned difficulties. Mr. Moerbauer, would you please look once again at the court warrant dated 15th March 1996 and issued by the court for the search of six apartments, six different addresses? Please, Mr. Moerbauer, can you confirm that in this court warrant at the bottom of the first page it is stated that there is an obligation for this court warrant to be handed to the person it is intended for immediately or within 24 hours at the latest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that here in the warrant.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you. Allow me to continue the cross-examination where we broke off before the break. Mr. Moerbauer, as you stated before this court, you took 30-50 documents for the purpose of photocopying them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The instructions for photocopying were given to you by your superior, Mr. Gschwendt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These documents were taken by you to another part of the building, where you photocopied them and made two copies; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When taking those 30-50 documents, you did not make any official inventory of those papers which you took with you to copy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I took the respective binders with me and two copies of the documents were made by myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was whether you made a precise list of those documents before copying them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the copying each binder only -- only each binder received a number, and the documents in the binders were not numbered at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Moerbauer, that yesterday testifying before this court you said that you took out the documents from the cardboard box or, rather, the binders, that you took them to be photocopied, and then you returned them, placing the originals back into the binders, and the copies on the -- placing the copies on the box where the binders used to be? Is that what you stated yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The copies -- the copies made, the second copies for the police, were between the binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that yesterday you did not say that you took the binders with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I took the individual binders with me for copying, binder by binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time you were copying them, you did not have the permission of the investigating judge to carry out such operations with the documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was -- Mr. Gschwendt asked me to copy these documents, and as far as I knew, this was done with the agreement of the investigating magistrate.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You, Mr. Moerbauer, never saw a document containing the approval of the magistrate -- judge, investigating judge, for such an operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no document, but notes were made regarding this. This was on 18th or maybe at the latest on 20th. Mr. Bycek consulted the judge at the time and this was confirmed by the judge, and a note on the record was made.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, is it true that Mr. Panzer on that day placed indications on the tapes of Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The seized videotapes of Mr. Mucic were labelled by Mr. Panzer, my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, you said that the other videotapes were labelled the following days. Is it correct that these videotapes were also labelled by your colleague, Mr. Panzer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Moerbauer, that Mr. Panzer was with you during the search in Taubergasse number 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My colleague Panzer was present at the search at Taubergasse 15, Door 10, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Panzer, your colleague, did not attend the search in the premises of Inda-Bau on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it is also correct that the following days he labelled all the videotapes which were in the Inda-Bau cardboard box?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Moerbauer, that the search of the premises and the seizure of objects was carried out on a Monday, on 18th March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you stated that you started reviewing the documents on Friday, 22nd March, together with an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that up to that day not a single document had any particular label on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only documents in the binders -- the individual documents in the binders were not individually numbered at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you said that you examined the documents in the period from March 22nd until April 2nd, together with an interpreter, and that when you had discovered what they contained, you gave them certain labels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every document -- the interpreter received each document from the different binders, and when the interpreter received the document, I gave it a number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you will agree with me that since the translation lasted until 2nd April, the last group of documents that you gave to the interpreter were numbered on 2nd April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, is it correct that in some reports, the Bericht, on information of seized documents you noted certain errors recording the number of seized videotapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Concerning the number of seized videotapes, the first note was items seized from Taubergasse 15, Door 14. The first error was discovered by a colleague and was corrected and the seized videotapes from Koppstrasse, Door number 14, this was discovered later, at a later stage, and was noted by me in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask you, Mr. Moerbauer, if you could look again at the report on search of the apartment in Taubergasse 15, the apartment of Mr. Zejnil Delalic and to look at the same time at this report, this Bericht, which I would like to be marked, shown to the Prosecutor and given to you for identification. Mr. Moerbauer, the record on the search of Mr. Delalic's apartment, that is the Niederschrift, does it say that 30 videotapes were seized in the apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does your record of 22nd April 1996 say that in Mr. Delalic's apartment 28 videotapes were found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Moerbauer, which policeman noticed the error in the number of videotapes in Mr. Delalic's apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't say. I only know on the same day there was a note on the record from Gruth (sic), or one of the colleagues who had seized these videotapes, and this note on the record should be in the court records.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, Mr. Moerbauer, the name of the videotapes which went missing between Mr. Delalic's apartment and your police station?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The name of the video cassettes? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The name of the video cassettes, they were 28 -- they were actually 28 video cassettes, and on the record 30 was noted. I can't give you the names of the 28 videotapes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, I'm not interested in the names of the 28, but in the names of the two videotapes. Can you tell me the names of the two videotapes that were numbered in the Niederschrift, that were listed in the Niederschrift, but which you did not receive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only 28 videotapes were handed over. In the record it was listed as -- they were given as 30 videotapes, and according to the colleagues this was a mistake and this was noted on the record on the same day. There were actually only 28 videotapes that I received, and this mistake was also included in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me the names of your colleagues who told you that this was merely an error?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The note was either made by my colleague Unger or by my colleague Winter -- Winkelmann -- Unger or Winkelmann. I'm not sure. I don't know if both signed this note, but this should be in the court files.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let me find out what might have happened. Did you put any identification marks on the 28th you recovered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as these videotapes go, the labelling was only put on in the following days. This is the gym bag that I took from Delalic's apartment and took to the police headquarters. Colleagues also came in there, wrote their report. I don't know if it was subsequently that they saw or how much subsequently they saw there was a mistake, but that same day they did enter that correction into the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Now if it was on the 28 you had an identifying by your own mark and then 30 were subsequently found, the two excess ones would not have those marks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, should there have been 30 videotapes, of course, they would not have been labelled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. If there are 30 and then you had marks on all the 30, then you might be wrong in saying there are 28. You see, if all of them had the marks you gave them on the date you took them, then the question of error might not have been made out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The various videos were viewed and they were referenced and then mentioned in the reports, and there were the analysis reports about the videos, and in those analysis reports, as far as I know, there were, in fact, only 28 videos, which were seized in that apartment, in the Taubergasse 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): In other words, Mr. Moerbauer, your colleagues Unger and Winkelman did not count correct and did not write down correct the items seized during the search in Taubergasse 15, that is in the apartment of Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's possible. It's also possible that there may have been an empty videotape case in among that number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, would you look again at the record, that is the Niederschrift, from the search of the Inda-Bau company, and please if at the same time I would like the Bericht to be shown to you from April 1996 after it has been marked and after it has been looked at by the Prosecution. I apologise. There are some translation markings in my handwriting on these documents. (Handed to Prosecution). (Handed to witness). Mr. Moerbauer, is it correct in this Niederschrift, which was drawn up on the search in the Inda-Bau company, it was stated that 51 video cassettes were seized without any further notification as to the videotapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 51 videotapes were not labelled in the course of the search. They were brought to the Vienna police headquarters in a box and Navrat handed them to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These video cassettes were marked in the following days by your colleague Panzer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your report, the Bericht of 22nd April 1996, you noted that on the Inda-Bau premises 54 video cassettes were discovered; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Panzer ascertained that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, is it correct that at the time when this error was discovered no witness of the witnesses who were present during the search at the Inda-Bau premises was present on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that on the occasion of the taking out of items -- the unmarked items from either the gym bag or the cardboard box neither Mr. Delalic or his official representatives were present, or any witness who in the report was marked as being present at that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you did not receive from your colleagues any items on which you would have signed off? You simply received a gym bag on the first occasion and an open cardboard box with items on the second?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, this may be a bit easier because this is regarding a larger number of video cassettes, in other words, the cassettes were not lost on their way. Can you please, Mr. Moerbauer, list exactly the video cassettes that were not registered on the premises of the Inda-Bau and were later described in your report; in other words, the exact names of the video cassettes which emerged was the difference between the state of affairs on the premises and the one that you described in your report of April 22nd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The videotapes from the Inda-Bau company, there were always 54 of them. There were apparently 54 of them. They were only counted later on when they were marked. Now with regard to a reference to them and giving them a name, that only happened later in the course of processing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, I'm looking at the second page of the Niederschrift from the Inda-Bau and to me it is obvious that it states there "51 cassettes". What I'm interested in is what three cassettes did you find later and what are the names of these cassettes? Can you tell me that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the box there were apparently always those 54 videotapes, but after handover they weren't counted. It was when we labelled them consecutively that we realised that there were 54 and not 51. Now they were not given a name at once. It was only in the course of the one and a half to two weeks of analysis that the contents of the videotapes was indicated in a report along with the contents -- along with the references -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, if this is correct, Mr. Moerbauer, your colleague who conducted the search at the Inda-Bau as well as its markings did his job conscientiously and properly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I did not quite get it. Was it "did" or "didn't conscientiously"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Could you repeat it? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr. Moerbauer, if what you say is correct that in the cardboard box there were always 54 video cassettes, are you thereby confirming that your colleagues who were on the premises incorrectly noted things down and therefore discharged their jobs without proper diligence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Do you want him to comment on that? I'm not sure he's in a very good position to say anything about it. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): The witness replied that no comment is necessary. We have 51 cassettes and then 54. Three video cassettes appeared from somewhere. I don't know where they appeared from, your Honours. Maybe the witness can help us in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: As time goes on, perhaps a proper inference might be drawn. You need not say it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How can he comment on any of it? The error is apparent. It seems somewhat a little strange that the two officers should be miscounting, one making 30 cassettes and they turn out to be 28, and one counting them as 51 and they turn out to be 54. So we can draw our own conclusions. You don't have to ask him and embarrass him. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Yes, your Honours. I'm only doing my cross-examination for now. Mr. Moerbauer, you stated before this Trial Chamber that you yourself reviewed about 60 cassettes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Watched videos, yes, watched 60 videos, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Moerbauer, that in none of these 60 video cassettes you did not find -- you found any cassettes that you were given a warrant by this Tribunal and which refer to the torture of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The report itself is very clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see any contents of that nature, but when it comes to investigations, we take both account of what is in the favour of the prosecution and what is in the favour of the defence. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr. Moerbauer, thank you for your care and for defending of the process, but did you note precisely that among the video cassettes that you reviewed there were no video cassettes that referred to the torture of prisoners, and that this was also part of the report that you drew up on April 22nd, 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now in the videotapes there was footage of a camp or camps and apparently prisoners were involved and they were visible on the videos, and one person, a prisoner no doubt, had to do push-ups.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, my question is about the video cassettes taken from Mr. Delalic's apartment and from the Inda-Bau.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was referring to all videos.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, if in your report of 22nd April 1996 you had written down that there were no such video cassettes, that is in the cassettes from the apartment of Mr. Zejnil Delalic and the Inda-Bau, then this is correct, what you wrote in this report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, the list of items that did not contain torture of prisoners and war crimes you did not submit to the State Prosecutor of Austria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The analysis report as well as the videotapes were transferred to the Vienna District Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You yourself numbered the items, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With regard to the numbering of the videotapes, that was done but my colleague, Panzer, but when it came to putting this together in the report, that's something I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the documents, to the papers. You did it yourself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reference of the written documents was -- the referencing of those documents was done by me and only by me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At no time, Mr. Moerbauer, was there an official inventory of the items, including several people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The documents after the 2nd April -- all the documents which had been seized and those that were relevant to the case were referenced and subsequently a summary report was drawn up about the contents of the various documents, but not all documents were translated and mentioned, because some documents were illegible and some documents were copies of others which were in a different file, and those kind of documents and some of the ID cards or identification papers, what have you, we didn't reference those and translate those.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your explanation, but that was not the gist of my question. My question was: was at any time before the referencing of items -- was there ever an official referencing either of the video cassettes, documents or other items?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Official listing as regards the individual documents, there was no such official listing. With regard to the videotapes and the referencing, that had been done, but the documents had not been listed individually at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Two more questions for today and then we can break. Please, at no time was the identification of any items done in the presence of Mr. Zejnil Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But he was not in Austria at that time, so how could that be done? You don't expect them to do something which is impossible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The person concerned, as far as the search warrant goes, was in each and every instance Zdravko Mucic. The search warrants had been issued in connection with Zdravko Mucic. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I'm only asking in regard of Mr. Delalic. Mr. Delalic was not present during any identification of items which were conducted subsequently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delalic was not present.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: His counsel was not present either, nor was he informed of this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Did he have a counsel at that stage? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: In Vienna? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I was in Sarajevo, in Munich and here and he did have a counsel in Germany.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: We are talking about his performance in Austria.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: In Vienna.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, in Vienna, not in Sarajevo or in Germany.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But were you his counsel in March 1992. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): As of April 1st, and the German counsel as of March 19th, and they were all in a position to have been informed and a foreigner according to the law, to the local laws, has the right to choose a counsel from the country of his origin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: He's a very accomplished man, the court interpreter. He knew what to do. I think, Ms. Residovic, you are losing control now. We'll reassemble tomorrow morning and you continue with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: --ooOoo--
